question: Should OpenClaw accept `sessions.diagnose` plus `openclaw sessions diagnose` as a durable public operator/client diagnosis contract in core?
rationale: The patch appears technically sound, but it adds a new supported Gateway method, CLI command, Swift model, finding vocabulary, and docs; automation cannot decide that long-term API/product commitment for maintainers.

options.title: Accept Diagnosis Contract
options.body: Land this additive read-only Gateway/CLI diagnosis surface as the supported operator path for session triage.

options.title: Narrow Vocabulary First
options.body: Trim result fields, finding codes, or CLI behavior before merge if maintainers want a smaller compatibility surface.

options.title: Defer From Core
options.body: Pause or close this PR if maintainers want the broader stuck-session diagnostics or recovery work to define the contract first.

recommendation.title: Accept Diagnosis Contract
recommendation.body: Land this additive read-only Gateway/CLI diagnosis surface as the supported operator path for session triage.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter Steinberger has the clearest history signal around adjacent session RPC/protocol and diagnostic-state surfaces.
